content: The estimated number of children newly infected with HIV through mother-to-child transmission is calculated among women living with HIV who have delivered within the past 12 months. To determine this, the following data is required: The estimated number of women living with HIV who gave birth, categorized by age group. The distribution of pregnant women living with HIV who are receiving antiretroviral therapy (ART), categorized by the timing of treatment initiation (before conception, early in pregnancy, or late in pregnancy). The proportion of pregnant women retained on ART at the time of delivery. The estimated incidence of HIV among pregnant and breastfeeding women. The distribution of women receiving ART postpartum (after delivery). Among women receiving ART, the percentage whose infants have ceased breastfeeding, categorized by the child’s age in months (from 0 to 35 months). Among women not receiving ART, the percentage whose infants have ceased breastfeeding, categorized by the child’s age in months (from 0 to 35 months). Among breastfeeding women receiving ART, the percentage who discontinue ART each month. The estimated incidence of HIV among breastfeeding women. The probabilities of mother-to-child transmission of HIV based on different ART regimens and infant feeding practices. The total number of people who have died from AIDS-related causes per 100,000 population is another critical indicator. This measures the impact of HIV prevention, care, and treatment programs. The rationale for this indicator is that, in the era of the Treat All approach, effective diagnosis and treatment of people living with HIV should significantly reduce deaths due to AIDS-related causes. To calculate this, the following components are used: Numerator: The estimated number of people who died from AIDS-related causes during the calendar year. Denominator: The total population, regardless of HIV status. The method of measurement involves mathematical modeling tools, such as Spectrum AIM. These tools require demographic data, HIV prevalence, the number of people receiving ART, HIV incidence, and assumptions about survival rates. Additional data from verbal autopsies and/or vital reporting systems (including estimates of underreporting and misclassification) may also be incorporated. Disaggregation of this data is performed by: Gender: Male, female, transgender. Age groups: 0–4, 5–9, 10–14, 15–19, 20–24, 25–49, 50+. Key populations: Men who have sex with men, people living in prisons or other closed settings, people who inject drugs, sex workers, and transgender individuals.
